11435.news: With Zach Charbonnet (ACL recovery) and rookie Jadarian Price (IR) out, Wilson ran 24 times for 100 yards and a touchdown and caught his only target for 15 yards in Seattle's 20-3 Sunday night win over Kansas City on Oct 25. He has 111 carries for 403 yards and three touchdowns this season. On Oct. 26, Mike Macdonald wouldn't commit to Charbonnet playing in Week 8, even though Charbonnet will practice fully this week. Seattle is also opening Price's 21-day practice window. Seattle plays at Chicago on Monday night, Nov. 2.
11435.take: Wilson showed he can handle a full workload, and fantasy analysts expect him to lead the backfield again if Charbonnet is held out or eased in. That makes him a reasonable flex for Monday night, but check Seattle's final injury report first. Once Charbonnet and Price are both back, his role will probably shrink to a committee or change-of-pace job. He's a short-term redraft asset and a low-value depth piece in dynasty, so sell him if anyone pays for this game.

9230.name: Tanner McKee
9230.headline: Mistake-filled MNF loss in Dallas; stays starter, Washington next
9230.news: McKee went 23-of-35 for 211 yards with a touchdown to Makai Lemon and an interception in the Eagles' 38-21 Monday night loss at Dallas on Oct 26, per the Eagles' box score (Yahoo's game story listed 20 completions). His fourth-quarter pick, thrown toward Dallas Goedert and caught by DeMarvion Overshown with Philadelphia down 10 and 7:55 left, ended the comeback. He was sacked twice. The Eagles have lost five straight and are 2-5, and local coverage is questioning Nick Sirianni's future. Hurts (blood clots) is expected out for the season. Joe Milton was the backup Monday with rookie Cole Payton inactive, and Philadelphia plays at Washington (1-4-1) on Sunday night, Nov. 1.
9230.take: His two starts have been similar: plenty of attempts, about 6 yards per attempt or less, and one touchdown per game. That gives him a floor in superflex but very little ceiling. Washington is a soft spot, so he's a usable superflex QB2 in Week 8 and a bench in 12-team 1QB leagues. A team losing this much could look at a change at some point, though nobody has announced one. In dynasty, he's a short-term starter with no long-term role, so a rebuilding team should move him to a superflex contender who needs a body.

13296.name: Caleb Douglas
13296.headline: Two TDs in ankle return; Patriots visit Miami next
13296.news: Douglas returned on Oct 25 from an ankle injury that had kept him out since Week 2. He caught 2 of 3 targets for 70 yards and two touchdowns in Miami's 28-25 win over the Jets. The first was a 7-yard catch from Malik Willis, his first NFL TD, and the second was a 63-yarder with under five minutes left that sealed the Dolphins' first win of the season. He had 7 catches for 113 yards through two games before the injury. Miami hosts New England on Sunday, Nov 1.
13296.take: The big-play ability is real, but two touchdowns on three targets won't repeat, and Miami's passing game with Willis is inconsistent. Treat him as a bench stash or deep-league WR5 until his targets rise, and don't chase the points against the Patriots. For a rebuilding dynasty team, he's a 6-foot-4 third-round rookie with a real path to starter snaps on a rebuilding offense. Buy him now while his price is low.

4892.name: Baker Mayfield
4892.headline: Back from thumb injury; barely needed to throw in 43-13 rout
4892.news: Mayfield returned on Oct. 25 after missing three games with a dislocated right thumb and went 7-of-11 for 64 yards and a touchdown in Tampa Bay's 43-13 win at Carolina. His only score was a 14-yard pass to Tez Johnson just before halftime. He threw only nine passes before the half, and the Bucs led 33-6 at the break. Bucky Irving did most of the work with 24 carries for 106 yards and two touchdowns. Emeka Egbuka (concussion, foot) missed the game. Tampa Bay (2-5) hosts Atlanta in Week 8, and previews say how his thumb holds up in practice is still worth watching.
4892.take: The box score doesn't tell us much because the game was a blowout and the Bucs ran the ball. Coming off a thumb injury, he'll have more to prove when a game is close. When healthy he's a mid-range QB1/QB2 in 1QB leagues, and he gets a solid matchup against Atlanta in Week 8, especially if Egbuka returns. For a 1-5 rebuilding dynasty team, he's a veteran who should be sold to a superflex contender now that he's healthy again.

13414.name: Kaelon Black
13414.headline: First career TD with CMC hurt; fumble cuts his workload
13414.news: With Christian McCaffrey hurt in the first quarter, Black led the 49ers in rushing during the 29-20 loss at Atlanta on Oct. 25. He had 12 carries for 63 yards, including a 30-yard run for his first career touchdown. He also lost a fumble and got only one more carry afterward, per one report. On Oct. 26, Kyle Shanahan said McCaffrey has a mild hamstring strain (it was first listed as a thigh injury) and the team is optimistic he'll be ready after the Week 8 bye. San Francisco hosts the Raiders in Week 9.
13414.take: Black is the clear backup to McCaffrey, and he was efficient as the lead runner. The fumble may have cost him snaps, though. Unless McCaffrey's hamstring lingers past the bye, Black goes back to a small role in Week 9. He's still one of the higher-value handcuffs because the 49ers' backfield produces big numbers and McCaffrey is 30 with a long injury history. In dynasty he's a cheap young back for a rebuilding team, so buy him at backup price. In redraft, stash him only if you have room.

8122.name: Zonovan Knight
8122.headline: Led Arizona's snaps without Love, but touches were light
8122.news: With rookie Jeremiyah Love (ankle) out again, Knight played 40 snaps to Tyler Allgeier's 35 (about 53%) in Arizona's 30-16 loss to Denver on Oct. 25. He ran 7 times for 48 yards and caught 3 passes. He also dropped a potential touchdown in the end zone, and Arizona settled for a field goal. Before the game, Mike LaFleur said Knight would get a lot of early-down work. He has described Allgeier as the complementary back for pass protection and short yardage, and he said Knight will keep a role when Love returns. Love's next chance to play is Week 8 at Dallas on Nov. 1. Arizona is 2-5.
8122.take: Knight had the bigger snap share, but 10 touches is a thin workload, and once Love is healthy he becomes a change-of-pace back at best. If Love sits again, Dallas is one of the weakest run defenses in the league, which would make Knight a low-end flex in deep leagues. Otherwise he's a bench stash. He's not a long-term piece for a rebuilding dynasty team.

9501.name: DeMario Douglas
9501.headline: Quiet Week 7 after hot streak; Dolphins up next
9501.news: Douglas caught 3 of 4 targets for 23 yards in New England's 30-24 Thursday night loss at Chicago on Oct 22. In the two games before that, with Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins out, he had 11 catches on 13 targets for 151 yards and three touchdowns. Doubs and Hollins remain on IR. Drake Maye threw for 321 yards and three TDs in the loss, and A.J. Brown also had a quiet night. The Patriots had extra rest and play at Miami on Sunday, Nov 1.
9501.take: The drop to four targets in Week 7 is a concern because his opportunities shrank even with Doubs and Hollins out, and his touchdown run was always going to cool off. He still projects as the No. 2 option next to Brown in an offense with a productive QB. Miami's defense is a good matchup, so he's a reasonable WR3/flex in 12-team leagues. In dynasty he's a smaller slot receiver on a modest contract with a capped ceiling, so if anyone is still paying for the two-game spike, take a pick for him.

4993.name: Mike Gesicki
4993.headline: Fifth TD; Erick All's knee injury could open targets
4993.news: Gesicki scored a touchdown in Cincinnati's Week 7 game against Baltimore on Oct 25, giving him five TDs on just 13 catches this season. I could not verify the rest of his stat line from that game. Fellow tight end Erick All Jr. hurt his right knee in the same game and did not return, and the Bengals have not given an update on how long he'll be out. All missed most of 2024 and all of 2025 after two surgeries on the same knee. A preview before the game described Gesicki as a strong start in three of his first five games, all in a part-time role.
4993.take: His scoring has been impressive, but 13 catches in six games is not enough volume to rely on, and touchdown rates like that usually come down. If All misses time, Gesicki becomes the clear receiving tight end, which would make him a streaming TE2 with TD upside in redraft. He's worth adding now and starting in a favorable matchup if All is ruled out. For a rebuilding dynasty team, he's a 31-year-old vet with little lasting value, so sell him if a contender pays anything for the touchdowns.
